hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Oceania, group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about three-quarters of the way from Hawaii to Australia || mostly mountainous islands of volcanic origin; narrow coastal plains || a Y-shaped chain of four main islands and 80 smaller islands; several of the islands have active volcanoes, including several underwater volcanoes || Resources: manganese, hardwood forests, fish || Exports: fish, ships, perfume plants, wood, copra (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: mostly mountainous islands of volcanic origin; narrow coastal plains || Oceania, group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, about three-quarters of the way from Hawaii to Australia

climate.excerpt: tropical; moderated by southeast trade winds from May to October; moderate rainfall from November to April; may be affected by cyclones from December to April || tropical cyclones (January to April); volcanic activity; volcanism also causes minor earthquakes; tsunamis volcanism: significant volcanic activity with multiple eruptions in recent years; Yasur (361 m), one of the world's most active volcanoes, has experienced continuous activity in recent centuries; other historically active volcanoes include Aoba, Ambrym, Epi, Gaua, Kuwae, Lopevi, Suretamatai, and Traitor's Head

economy.excerpt: lower-middle income Pacific island economy; extremely reliant on subsistence agriculture and tourism; environmentally fragile; struggling post-pandemic and Tropical Cyclone Harold rebound; sizeable inflation; road infrastructure aid from Australia || Exports: fish, ships, perfume plants, wood, copra (2023) || Industries: food and fish freezing, wood processing, meat canning
